name: agentic-state-loop
description: Harnessed autonomous agent loop: an agent executes each cycle, one cycle is at most one atomic Git commit, canonical state is schema-validated JSON (SSOT), and rule-based invariants are enforced mechanically by Claude Code hooks/permissions. The judgment/state engine is the vendored Lean binary asl-loop, built from source in the instance.

files.note: the loop instance: scripts/, schema.json, prompts/, lean/ (source of the asl-loop engine binary — build it to <loop_dir>/bin/asl-loop with `just engine-build`; scripts, hooks and permissions all run this engine), tmp/, .gitignore.
the enforcement harness: settings.json (hooks run <loop_dir>/bin/asl-loop hook <event>). If the target already has .claude/, merge (do not clobber) and re-verify every deny still holds.
human convenience layer; merge into an existing justfile instead of overwriting

lock_format.source_sha256: <output of: bin/<tool> recipe hash agentic-state-loop, run in the control plane>

parameters.name: loop_dir
parameters.fills: every __ASL_LOOP_DIR__ token in the installed files
parameters.guidance: Directory name of the loop instance inside the target. Keep the default unless it collides.

parameters.name: documents
parameters.guidance: The domain state files: one entry per canonical JSON document with `seed` (initial content) and `schema` (JSON Schema subset). Derive the shape from what the product's loop must track — queues, ledgers, cursors, findings. Every document the cycle prompt tells the agent to update must be declared here so validate covers it.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.guidance: stop_after_idle_cycles / stop_after_failed_runs / max_session_cycles as positive integers. Defaults are sane; tighten for expensive cycles.

parameters.name: logs
parameters.guidance: Extra append-only .jsonl ledgers beside the built-in runs.jsonl (default: journal.jsonl, which the cycle prompt appends to). Appends go through `asl-loop state append-log`; only declared logs are writable that way.

parameters.name: protected_paths
parameters.guidance: Target-relative paths/globs only a human may change (the product's own canon files, if any). The guard hook denies agent writes and cycle commits exclude them; a human resume checkpoint records their diffs. Also mirror them as static deny entries in .claude/settings.json where practical.

parameters.name: deny_rules
parameters.guidance: Extra mechanical fences derived from the project's stated prohibitions (e.g. a "never touch legacy/" constraint becomes the path pattern `^legacy/`; a "no new dependencies" constraint becomes an install-command pattern). Patterns are a restricted glob dialect — literal characters, `*`, leading `^`, trailing `$`, substring-search semantics — NOT regexes; see the recipe README's conversion table. `asl-loop state validate` warns on legacy-regex lookalikes.

parameters.name: domain_instructions
parameters.guidance: What one cycle of THIS product's work is: selection -> execution -> verification -> state update, written against the declared documents. Keep the surrounding harness constraints intact.

parameters.name: verify_allows
parameters.guidance: Allow entries for the domain's verification commands the cycle prompt tells the agent to run (e.g. "Bash(npm test*)", "Bash(pytest*)"). Without them a non-interactive cycle auto-denies every verification command and step 5 of the cycle prompt cannot execute. Add only deterministic verification commands; never remove or weaken the deny set.

post_install_checks: grep ASL-PARAMETER-UNFILLED <loop_dir>/schema.json <loop_dir>/prompts/cycle.md returns nothing (the scripts define the marker constant; only the parameter surfaces must be clean) and no __ASL_LOOP_DIR__ token survives in any installed file

just engine-build succeeds (builds <loop_dir>/lean/ with lake and installs <loop_dir>/bin/asl-loop; network only for the pinned elan toolchain download) and <loop_dir>/bin/asl-loop version prints the engine version
Claude Code trust is accepted for the target root (hooks are otherwise not enforced)
